questions.question: In Zurich, what JavaScript standard is now supported for server-side scripting, enabling async/await patterns?

explanation.correct: Zurich expands scripting capabilities with support for ECMAScript 2021 (ES12). This enables developers to use async/await patterns, making external API calls cleaner and non-blocking.

wrongAnswers.A: ES6 was supported in earlier releases.
wrongAnswers.B: ES9 is not the Zurich scripting upgrade.
wrongAnswers.D: ES14 support is not mentioned in Zurich release notes.

questions.question: Which new Zurich feature allows developers to isolate their work and merge changes via Git without affecting other developers?

explanation.correct: Developer Sandboxes in Zurich give each developer an isolated environment. They can work on their own Git branches, commit changes, and merge back into the shared dev instance.

wrongAnswers.A: Scoped Applications provide isolation at the app level, not developer-level Git workflows.
wrongAnswers.C: Personal Developer Instances (PDIs) are free instances, not the new Zurich Git-integrated sandboxes.
wrongAnswers.D: Update Set Branches is not a Zurich feature.

questions.question: What new App Engine Studio capability in Zurich allows developers to generate subflows from uploaded images?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces AI-Assisted Development features, including the ability to create subflows from sketches or uploaded images in App Engine Studio.

wrongAnswers.A: Flow Generator is not the specific feature name.
wrongAnswers.C: While descriptive, Sketch-to-Subflow is not the official Zurich terminology.
wrongAnswers.D: Visual Flow Import is not the correct feature name.

questions.question: Which new Zurich tool helps developers measure form load times and identify slow widgets or scripts?

explanation.correct: Performance Analyzer in Zurich helps developers measure form load times, trace performance issues, and identify slow widgets or scripts.

wrongAnswers.A: Script Profiler is not the Zurich feature name.
wrongAnswers.C: Widget Debugger is not the specific Zurich performance tool.
wrongAnswers.D: Load Time Monitor is not the correct feature name.

questions.question: In Zurich Flow Designer, what feature allows trigger definitions (endpoint, schema, security) to be saved and reused?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces Saved External Triggers where trigger definitions including endpoint, schema, and security settings can be saved and reused across flows.

wrongAnswers.A: Trigger Templates is not the official Zurich terminology.
wrongAnswers.C: Reusable Actions are for flow actions, not triggers.
wrongAnswers.D: Trigger Library is not the correct feature name.

questions.question: What new UI Builder feature in Zurich automatically binds data to components?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces Auto Data Binding in UI Builder, which automatically binds data to components along with AI-driven design suggestions.

wrongAnswers.A: Smart Binding is not the official Zurich feature name.
wrongAnswers.C: Dynamic Binding existed before; Auto Data Binding is the new Zurich feature.
wrongAnswers.D: Data Link is not the correct feature name.

questions.question: Which Zurich ATF (Automated Testing Framework) improvement provides better insights when tests fail?

explanation.correct: Zurich ATF gains better Failure Insights and a more configurable workspace for test authoring, making it easier to diagnose why tests fail.

wrongAnswers.A: Enhanced Test Logs is not the specific Zurich improvement.
wrongAnswers.C: Debug Mode is not the ATF-specific Zurich feature.
wrongAnswers.D: Test Replay is not the highlighted Zurich ATF feature.

questions.question: What IntegrationHub enhancement in Zurich adds support for newer scripting capabilities?

explanation.correct: Zurich IntegrationHub adds PowerShell v6+ support along with improved SOAP security for enterprise integrations.

wrongAnswers.A: Python 3 Support is not the highlighted Zurich IntegrationHub feature.
wrongAnswers.C: Node.js Integration is not mentioned as a Zurich enhancement.
wrongAnswers.D: Ruby Support is not a Zurich feature.
